name: VITUR Tourist visa / visa-free entry

requirements.blocker_text: Covers tourism and similar short visits; working in Brazil on a tourist visa or visa-free entry violates Lei 13.445/2017 (the Migration Law), even for remote work performed for a non-Brazilian employer -- the dedicated Digital Nomad route exists specifically to legalise that scenario.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the relevant work or digital-nomad route instead if any form of paid activity is intended.

requirements.blocker_text: Many nationalities enter visa-free or via eVisa for stays up to 90 days, extendable once for another 90 days (180 days total per 12-month period); other nationalities need a consular VITUR visa.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for a VITUR visa at a Brazilian consulate if not visa-free or eVisa eligible.

evidence_required.document: Passport valid for the intended stay
Proof of onward/return travel and sufficient funds where requested at the border

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days, extendable once to 180 days per 12-month period

sources.title: Ministério das Relações Exteriores (gov.br/mre) -- consular services pages describing Brazilian visa categories and the 90+90 day stay structure for visa-free/eVisa entrants

notes: Overstaying triggers fines of R$100/day (capped at R$10,000) and potential re-entry restrictions, per multiple independent sources cross-checked in this research pass. Change of status to a long-term category from inside Brazil while on tourist status is generally not permitted for most categories -- applicants typically need to apply for the target visa from outside Brazil, though some routes (e.g. the Digital Nomad visa) explicitly allow in-country status change via the Federal Police's MigranteWeb platform, a genuine exception worth flagging since it isn't the default pattern.
